summary:
SPACE EXPLORER: Beyond the Universe is an interactive 3D educational space game and Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer built for students aged 7 and above. Before developing our solution, our team (Aliens from Mars) surveyed students and found that traditional space science often feels too abstract and disconnected from real world exploration.
To address this challenge, we transformed verified NASA open datasets including NASA Open APIs, DONKI, OSDR, RadLab, and Mars Trek into hands on, playable missions. Players explore a NASA Eyes inspired 3D solar system, choose from four distinct mission specialists across Beginner, Intermediate, and Advanced difficulty tiers, inspect real historical spacecraft from Sputnik 1 to Orion in a 3D hangar, and survive realistic deep space emergencies like solar storms and radiation exposure.
By turning authentic astrophysics and spaceflight history into an engaging, accessible simulation with an upcoming AI Mission Video Studio for student creations our project inspires the next generation of young explorers to understand and experience real space science

a 3D educational space exploration web application developed using AI assisted development with Gemini 4 Hydrogen.
The application uses React and TypeScript for the frontend, Three.js and WebGL for 3D graphics, Node.js for backend operations, and Vite as the build tool

CSS and HTML handle the website's presentation and structure. The Web Audio API provides sound effects, while local Storage saves game progress.
We used Playwright and automated unit tests for verification. Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash was planned for AI-powered video generation.

SPACE EXPLORER: Beyond the Universe is an interactive 3D educational game and Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer built for students aged 7 and above. Instead of just reading facts on a screen, players step directly into a live, NASA Eyes-inspired 3D solar system where they can orbit, zoom, inspect planetary telemetry, and switch between scaled views and real Astronomical Unit (AU) distances

Players start by selecting one of four mission specialists matched to their skill level—Cadet Nova (Beginner), Dr. Elena Vance (Scientist — Intermediate), Cmdr. Marcus Reed (Researcher — Advanced), or Zeph-7 (a fictional alien companion who sparks imaginative thinking while staying clearly separate from real NASA science). From there, players explore historical spacecraft from Sputnik 1 (1957) to Orion / Artemis I (2022) in a 3D Hangar and Timeline, earn virtual coins through missions and quizzes in the Learning Centre, and take on deep-space missions to the Moon, Mars, and Jupiter. During missions, players scan cratered surfaces for safe landings, repair damaged spacecraft systems, and make real-time survival decisions during solar storms and radiation alerts.

Our goal is to bridge that gap by letting students learn astrophysics, orbital mechanics, and spaceflight history by actually experiencing them. By offering three difficulty tiers and clear scientific explanations whenever a player makes a mistake, the platform supports both young beginners and older students-helping inspire the next generation of explorers, researchers, and engineers worldwide.
